# Glossary — terms as the code uses them

- **ticket** — a work item; row in `tickets`. Only lifecycle: open → closed (no reopen).
- **priority** — `low` | `med` | `high` (DB vocabulary, `ticketd/db/schema.sql:5`). Clients
  also send numeric aliases `"1"/"2"/"3"` (and integers, stringified) which the API coerces
  (`ticketd/app/server.py:47-49`). The alias set is part of the frozen API surface. Note the
  code says `med`, not `medium` — the string is load-bearing in responses and the DB CHECK.
- **status** — `open` | `closed`. Exact strings; DB-enforced.
- **slug** — lowercased, non-alphanumerics collapsed to `-`, trimmed, max 64 chars
  (`ticketd/app/util.py:6`). Derived from title at create; not unique; apparently decorative
  (no read path) — OQ-003.
- **watcher** — implied audience of close notifications; in code it is only the hardcoded
  address `watchers@example.internal` (`ticketd/app/server.py:76`). There is no watchers table
  or subscription mechanism — "watcher" is vocabulary from the mailbox name only.
- **reset token** — see docs/domain/reset-token.md. "Token" in responses/emails means the
  32-hex presentable secret; the rewrite splits presentable token vs stored hash (PB-002).
- **bypass header** — `X-Internal-Bypass: 1` skips reset rate limiting
  (`ticketd/app/server.py:84`, comment: "undocumented"). Intent unknown (OQ-004).
- **internal export** — `/internal/export/csv`, a 3-column CSV (id,title,status — note: NOT
  all columns despite `SELECT *`; `ticketd/app/server.py:113-115`), unescaped commas in titles
  break the format. Written for the 2020 audit; liveness unknown (OQ-001).

No user-vocabulary conflicts are recordable: no user-facing docs or humans were available
(degraded intake). Conflicts, if any, surface when the owner reviews the guide.
